analysis: Examined base_text lines 1-911 of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift (units :2, :3). Head changes visible via patch: new closures stopsAsked/serveUnlessStopped (head 77-78); execute() now routes status replies through followerStatus, adding reply.stopsAsked = currentStopsAsked() alongside start progress (head 399-408); forwarded .serve now calls localServe(unlessStoppedSince: request.stopsBefore) (head 464-465). Later changed ranges (head 1459-2597) are outside these units and were not seen. Security relevance: forwarded control requests arrive over the paired link control channel (pairing-key authenticated per otherMacAnswers comment, base 267-269); the paired peer can already request serve/stop, so adding a stop-counter guard that can only suppress a serve does not grant new authority. stopsAsked is a counter exposed in status to the paired peer only; no secret, prompt (A-001) or key material involved. Cluster onboarding is not covered by specific canonical threats (closest TB-002/TB-003/A-018 availability). A malicious paired peer sending a stopsBefore value could at most prevent serving on the leader, which it could already do via .stop. Integration should verify localServe(unlessStoppedSince:) and currentStopsAsked implementations (head ~1459+, 2238+, 2573+) handle nil/old-peer values safely and that stop counters are persisted under the setup store's owner-only protections; no regression identified in reviewed scope.
